fullPassage: Imagine you are pedalling your bicycle on a level road. You stop pedalling: no force is now acting to move you forward. What happens? You gradually slow down. How could you slow down more suddenly, in a shorter distance? By putting the brakes on. Because the brakes change your movement, making you slow down more suddenly, they must be exerting a force on the bicycle and you, as they grip and rub on the wheel-rims. This is the force called friction, which tends to slow down moving things by acting in the direction opposite to movement, that is backwards. Even without the brakes on, there are other friction forces acting on you and your bicycle, which also slow you down. One of these is friction in the wheels rubbing on the axles. Another is air resistance, which you can feel, pushing you backwards as you and the bicycle move forwards. When you apply these ideas to something around you, like a cart, you can see what could be generating friction: mainly the axles rubbing on the body as they rotate.

❌② 일치: 'friction in the wheels rubbing on the axles'에서 바퀴가 축에 문질리는 마찰을 언급했어요.
❌③ 일치: 'Even without the brakes on, there are other friction forces ... which also slow you down'과 맞아요.
❌④ 일치: 'mainly the axles rubbing on the body as they rotate'와 맞아요.
det.tip: friction = slow down(느리게) → '빠르게'는 반대

ch: 마찰은 움직이는 물체를 더 빠르게 만드는 힘이다.
바퀴가 축에 문질리는 것도 자전거에 작용하는 마찰의 하나다.
브레이크를 쓰지 않아도 자전거를 느리게 하는 힘들이 존재한다.
수레에서는 주로 축이 몸체에 문질리며 회전할 때 마찰이 생긴다.

questions.passage: Imagine you are pedalling your bicycle on a level road. You stop pedalling: no force is now acting to move you forward. What happens? You gradually slow down. How could you slow down more suddenly, in a shorter distance? By ①<u>putting</u> the brakes on. Because the brakes change your movement, making you slow down more suddenly, they must be ②<u>exerting</u> a force on the bicycle and you, as they grip and rub on the wheel-rims. This is the force called friction, which tends to slow down moving things by acting in the direction opposite to movement, that is backwards. Even without the brakes on, there are other friction forces acting on you and your bicycle, which also slow you down. One of these is friction in the wheels ③<u>rubbing</u> on the axles. Another is air resistance, which you can feel, pushing you backwards as you and the bicycle move forwards. When you apply these ideas to something around you, like a cart, you can see what could be ④<u>generated</u> friction: mainly the axles rubbing on the body as they rotate.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ generated → generating: 'could be + -ing'의 능동 진행이 필요
det.analysis:
✅ ① putting: 'By putting the brakes on'의 전치사 by + 동명사 — 적절
✅ ② exerting: 'must be exerting'의 진행 능동 — 적절
✅ ③ rubbing: 'the wheels rubbing'의 현재분사 — 적절
❌ ④ generated → generating: 뒤에 목적어 friction이 있어 '마찰을 발생시키고 있는' 능동 진행이므로 'could be generating'이어야 함 ←정답
det.tip: could be + -ing(generating) = 능동 진행
